name: HTML I — Fundamentals
description: Master foundational HTML5 document structure, headings, copy formatting, lists, links, images, and build your Personal Developer Portfolio.
whatYouLearn: Format copy with headings, lists, and semantic tags
Create links, images, and tabular data
Build a production Personal Developer Portfolio

exercises.title: DOCTYPE & Document Shell
exercises.description: Build a valid HTML5 document shell with DOCTYPE, html, head, title, and body.
exercises.theory: Every HTML5 document starts with <!DOCTYPE html> to trigger standard browser rendering.
exercises.solutionCode: Welcome to Web Development
hints: Doctype must be the first line

exercises.title: Headings Hierarchy
exercises.description: Structure page headers using H1 through H6 tags.
exercises.theory: Headings define document outline. Use H1 for main page title and H2-H6 for sub-sections.

exercises.title: Paragraphs & Formatting
exercises.description: Format text copy with p, strong, and em elements.
exercises.theory: defines paragraphs. denotes semantic importance; denotes emphasis.
exercises.objective: Format copy with p, strong, and em.
exercises.solutionCode:
ByteCode provides interactive learning for developers.

Practice directly in your browser.

exercises.title: Lists (ul & ol)
exercises.description: Create unordered bulleted and ordered numbered lists.
exercises.theory: <ul> creates bulleted lists, <ol> creates numbered lists, and <li> wraps items.
hints: li must be child of ul or ol

exercises.title: Hyperlinks & Target
exercises.description: Create clickable links using anchor tags and href attributes.
exercises.theory: <a> tags create hyperlinks. Use target='_blank' for external links.

exercises.title: Image Embedding & Alt Text
exercises.description: Embed images using img tag, src, and descriptive alt text.
exercises.theory: The tag embeds images. alt supplies fallback text for accessibility.
exercises.objective: Embed image with src and alt.

exercises.title: Line Breaks & Divider Lines
exercises.description: Format line separation using br and hr self-closing tags.
exercises.theory:
inserts inline line breaks;
creates horizontal thematic dividers.
exercises.objective: Add line break and divider line.

exercises.title: Generic Containers (div)
exercises.description: Group elements into block-level div containers.
exercises.theory: <div> is a generic block container used to group elements for layout styling.
exercises.objective: Wrap card elements inside a div container.

exercises.title: Inline Containers (span)
exercises.description: Format specific inline text words using span elements.
exercises.theory: <span> is an inline container used to style specific words within text without creating new lines.
hints: span does not cause line breaks

exercises.title: HTML Comments
exercises.description: Write developer documentation comments using <!-- comment --> syntax.
exercises.theory: Comments <!-- comment --> are ignored by browser rendering engines.
hints: Comments are visible in View Source

exercises.title: Preformatted Code Blocks
exercises.description: Render monospaced code blocks using pre and code tags.
exercises.theory: <pre> preserves whitespace formatting; <code> formats text monospaced.
requirements: Wrap code tag in pre tag

exercises.title: Quotes & Citations
exercises.description: Format block quotes and citations using blockquote and cite.
exercises.theory: <blockquote> formats multi-line quotes; <cite> attributes the citation source.
exercises.solutionCode:
Simplicity is prerequisite for reliability.

Edsger Dijkstra
requirements: Use blockquote tag with cite attribute

exercises.title: Superscript & Subscript
exercises.description: Format exponents and chemical formulas using sup and sub.
exercises.theory: <sub> renders subscript lower; <sup> renders superscript higher.
exercises.objective: Format H2O formula and E=mc2 equation.

exercises.title: Buttons & Action Controls
exercises.description: Create action buttons using button tags.
exercises.theory: <button> creates interactive buttons with type='button' or 'submit'.

exercises.title: Abbreviations & Tooltips
exercises.description: Format acronyms with hover tooltips using abbr tag.
exercises.theory: <abbr> formats acronyms; the title attribute displays hover tooltips.

exercises.title: Basic Data Tables
exercises.description: Create data tables using table, tr, th, and td tags.
exercises.theory: Tables format tabular data row-by-row with <tr> rows, <th> headers, and <td> cells.
requirements: Use tr, th, and td tags
hints: th headers are bold by default

exercises.title: Semantic Header & Footer
exercises.description: Structure top branding and bottom copyright with header and footer tags.
exercises.theory: <header> holds intro content; <footer> contains copyright and contact info.

exercises.title: HTML Entities & Escaping
exercises.description: Render reserved symbols (<, >, &) using HTML entities.
exercises.theory: Use < for <, > for >, and & for & to render reserved characters.
exercises.solutionCode: Use <div> tags to group content & layout elements.

exercises.title: Iframe Page Embedding
exercises.description: Embed external documents securely using iframe tag.
exercises.theory: <iframe> embeds external content. Always supply title for accessibility.

exercises.title: Capstone Project: Developer Personal Portfolio Website
exercises.description: Build a complete Personal Portfolio Website featuring header, bio, project lists, tables, and contact links.
exercises.theory: Combines all HTML I fundamentals into a complete production developer portfolio.
